mainTopic: How the משמרות shared the offerings of סוכות and the רגלים, and the meaning of the 70 פרים
overview: The first משנה explains how all 24 משמרות of כהנים shared the many מוסף offerings of סוכות. Each day the number of פרים drops by one, so more watches are free to share the 14 כבשים, until on the seventh day every watch brings exactly one animal. On שמיני עצרת they go back to the regular פייס, and the פרים rotate so no watch brings them two days in a row. The גמרא asks whether this fits only רבי or also the חכמים, who give the שמיני עצרת bull to one of the two watches that brought only two פרים, and it shows that both views work. רבי אלעזר then teaches that the 70 פרים stand for the 70 nations and the single פר of שמיני עצרת stands for ישראל, and the גמרא illustrates this with a parable of a king's great feast and small private meal. רבי יוחנן mourns that the nations lost this atonement when the בית המקדש was destroyed. A new משנה teaches that on the three רגלים all the משמרות share equally in the festival portions and the לחם הפנים, while the scheduled watch keeps the regular offerings. The גמרא explains what 'אימורי הרגלים' means and brings a verse limiting the equal sharing to the רגלים. It then begins asking for the source for sharing the לחם הפנים, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The animals offered on the first day of סוכות
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the large animals of the first day's מוסף: 13 פרים, 2 אילים, and 1 שעיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: MISHNAH: On the first festival day of Sukkot there were thirteen bulls, two rams, and one goat.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens by counting the big animals offered on the first day of סוכות. This sets up the math for how the 24 משמרות will share the work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah (במדבר כ״ט) requires 13 פרים, 2 אילים, 1 שעיר and 14 כבשים on day one. Each of these 16 non-sheep animals goes to its own watch, so 16 of the 24 משמרות are already busy. The משנה is building toward the question of what the remaining 8 watches do.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (the text of the משנה being studied)
'The Festival', the standard name for סוכות
Male goat (here a חטאת, a sin-offering)

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
On the first festival day of Sukkot
there were thirteen bulls there,
phrases.notes: As במדבר כ״ט lays out, the bulls drop by one each day: 13, 12, 11, and so on down to 7.

phrases.english: two rams and one goat.
phrases.notes: 13 + 2 + 1 = 16 animals, so 16 משמרות each bring one.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל חַג הָיוּ שָׁם שְׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר פָּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opening of a new משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On day one, 16 large offerings (13 bulls, 2 rams, 1 goat) occupy 16 of the 24 watches.

steps.title: Splitting fourteen sheep among the eight remaining watches
steps.stepSummary: The 14 כבשים go to the 8 leftover משמרות: six watches bring two sheep each, and two watches bring one each.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fourteen sheep remained for eight watches. On the first day, six watches offer two each, and the rest offer one each.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now handles the 14 sheep that are still left after the bulls, rams and goat were assigned. It divides them fairly among the 8 watches that have nothing yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are 14 sheep and only 8 watches, so not everyone can bring just one. Six watches bring two each (12 sheep) and the remaining two bring one each (2 sheep), which adds up to 14. This becomes the model for every following day.

keyTerms.meaning: The priestly watches (24 groups of כהנים)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Six offer two each' means six of the 8 leftover watches, not six watches total. The other 16 watches are already busy with the bulls, rams and goat.

phrases.english: Fourteen sheep remained there
for eight watches.

phrases.aramaic: בְּיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן, שִׁשָּׁה מַקְרִיבִין שְׁנַיִם שְׁנַיִם.
phrases.english: On the first day, six offer two each.
And the rest offer one each.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִשְׁתַּיְּירוּ שָׁם אַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר כְּבָשִׂים לִשְׁמוֹנֶה מִשְׁמָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Assigns the leftover sheep after the large animals were assigned in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Day one: 6 watches bring 2 sheep each and 2 watches bring 1 sheep each.

steps.title: The sheep distribution on the second and third days
steps.stepSummary: As the פרים decrease, more watches are free. On day two five watches bring two sheep each, and on day three four watches do.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the second day, five offer two each, and the rest one each. On the third day, four offer two each, and the rest one each.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the same pattern for days two and three of סוכות. Each day one fewer watch brings two sheep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Day two has 12 bulls, so 15 watches are busy and 9 are free: 5×2 + 4×1 = 14. Day three has 11 bulls, so 14 are busy and 10 are free: 4×2 + 6×1 = 14. One fewer bull means one more free watch, so one fewer watch needs to bring double.

phrases.english: On the second day, five offer two each.
And the rest offer one each.
On the third day, four offer two each.
And the rest offer one each.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּשֵּׁנִי, חֲמִשָּׁה מַקְרִיבִין שְׁנַיִם שְׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the day-one pattern to days two and three
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Day two: 5 watches bring double. Day three: 4 watches bring double. All other free watches bring one sheep.

steps.title: The sheep distribution on the fourth, fifth and sixth days
steps.stepSummary: The pattern continues: on days four, five and six, three, two and then one watch bring two sheep, and everyone else free brings one.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the fourth day, three offer two each, and the rest one each. On the fifth, two offer two each, and the rest one each. On the sixth, one offers two, and the rest one each.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes counting down the 'double' watches for days four through six. Each day there is one fewer watch bringing two sheep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Day four (10 bulls): 11 free watches, 3×2 + 8×1 = 14. Day five (9 bulls): 12 free, 2×2 + 10×1 = 14. Day six (8 bulls): 13 free, 1×2 + 12×1 = 14.

phrases.english: On the fourth day, three offer two each.
And the rest offer one each.
On the fifth day, two offer two each.
And the rest offer one each.
On the sixth day, one offers two.
And the rest offer one each.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּרְבִיעִי, שְׁלֹשָׁה מַקְרִיבִין שְׁנַיִם שְׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the countdown from step 3
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Days 4, 5 and 6 have 3, 2 and 1 double-bringing watches respectively.

steps.title: Seventh day all equal, and the eighth day goes back to the lottery
steps.stepSummary: On day seven every watch brings exactly one animal. On שמיני עצרת the watches return to the regular פייס, as on the other רגלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the seventh day they are all equal. On the eighth day they returned to the lottery, as on the other festivals.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה reaches the end of the countdown, where everything evens out on day seven. It then explains that שמיני עצרת works differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Day seven has 7 bulls + 2 rams + 1 goat = 10 animals, leaving 14 watches for 14 sheep, so all 24 watches bring one each. On שמיני עצרת there are only 1 bull, 1 ram, 1 goat and 7 sheep. There are too few offerings to give every watch one, so they use the normal פייס, just like on פסח and שבועות.

keyTerms.meaning: The lottery used to assign Temple tasks

steps.confusionAlert: 'All equal' on day seven means all 24 watches, including those offering bulls, rams or the goat, each bring exactly one animal. It does not refer only to the sheep watches.

phrases.english: On the seventh day, they are all equal.
phrases.notes: 10 large animals + 14 sheep = 24 offerings for 24 watches.

phrases.english: On the eighth day, they returned to the lottery
phrases.notes: שמיני עצרת has only 10 offerings in total.

phrases.english: as on the other festivals.

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּשְּׁבִיעִי, כּוּלָּן שָׁוִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the seven-day countdown and contrasts it with the eighth day
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Day 7: each watch brings one. Day 8: the standard lottery is used.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that שמיני עצרת is treated as a separate festival with its own system, not as an eighth day of סוכות.

steps.title: Rotation rule: the bull offerings rotate among the watches
steps.stepSummary: A watch that offered פרים today does not offer them tomorrow. Instead the assignments rotate so every watch gets a turn.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: whoever offered bulls today shall not offer bulls tomorrow; rather, they rotate in turn.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a fairness rule about which watch gets the bulls on each day of סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the משנה only said how many offerings each watch brings, not which animals. Bulls are the most prestigious offering. So a watch that brought a bull today moves to a different offering tomorrow, and the jobs cycle around so that everyone gets a share.

keyTerms.meaning: They rotate in a circle / take turns

steps.whatToRemember: On each of the first seven days of סוכות, all 24 משמרות share the מוסף. As the bulls decrease, more watches share the 14 sheep, until day seven when each watch brings exactly one. Bulls rotate so no watch brings them two days in a row. On שמיני עצרת they return to the regular פייס.

phrases.english: They said:
Whoever offered bulls today
shall not offer them tomorrow,
rather, they rotate in turn.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ: מִי שֶׁהִקְרִיב פָּרִים הַיּוֹם לֹא יַקְרִיב לְמָחָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a rule about which animals each watch offers, on top of the counts given in steps 1–5
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bull offerings rotate daily among the watches; no watch brings bulls two days in a row.

steps.title: Does our משנה follow only רבי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by suggesting that the משנה's rule of returning to the regular פייס on שמיני עצרת matches רבי and not the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Shall we say our משנה follows רבי and not the חכמים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking which תנא our משנה follows. This line sets up the next step, where a ברייתא will show the two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that on שמיני עצרת the watches return to the regular lottery. The גמרא suspects this fits only one side of a מחלוקת, which it is about to quote.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say (introduces a suggestion the גמרא may later reject)

phrases.english: Gemara:
Shall we say our Mishnah is according to Rabbi
and not according to the Rabbis?

steps.triggerLanguage: נֵימָא מַתְנִיתִין רַבִּי הִיא וְלָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה's rules to asking whose opinion the שמיני עצרת rule follows.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה's lottery on שמיני עצרת fits only רבי.

steps.title: The ברייתא: lottery for everyone, or only the two watches
steps.stepSummary: רבי says there is a fresh lottery for the שמיני עצרת bull. The חכמים say one of the two watches that did not bring three פרים offers it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: the bull brought on שמיני עצרת is decided by a new lottery from the start, says רבי. The חכמים say one of the two watches that did not bring three bulls offers it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to back up its suggestion. רבי wants a full new lottery, while the חכמים give the bull to one of two specific watches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Over סוכות there are 70 פרים and 24 watches, so 22 watches bring three and two watches bring only two. The חכמים give the שמיני עצרת bull to one of those two watches, which seems to leave no room for a regular lottery. That is why the משנה's 'return to the פייס' looks like רבי only.

keyTerms.meaning: The single bull of שמיני עצרת
Did a third time (brought a third bull)
From the start, as a fresh lottery

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
The bull that comes on the eighth day —
they draw lots over it from the start,
these are the words of Rabbi.
And the Sages say:
one of the two watches
that did not bring bulls a third time,
offers it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the suggestion in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה's lottery on שמיני עצרת matches רבי only.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא recording the מחלוקת between רבי and the חכמים.

steps.title: Even the חכמים need a lottery between two watches
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion is rejected: even according to the חכמים, the two eligible watches must draw lots to decide which one offers the bull.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows the חכמים. Do you think the two watches don't need a lottery?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back and says the משנה can fit the חכמים too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים only narrow the lottery down to two watches. A lottery is still needed to pick between them, so the משנה's mention of a פייס fits both opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say (a rejection that saves both opinions)
Is that to say? (a rhetorical challenge)

phrases.english: You can even say it is the Rabbis;
is that to say that two watches
do not need to draw lots?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן, אַטּוּ שְׁתֵּי מִשְׁמָרוֹת לָא אַפּוֹסֵי בָּעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of steps 7 and 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Full rejection of the claim that the משנה follows only רבי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed the חכמים need no lottery at all, but two candidates still need a פייס.
steps.whatToRemember: Both רבי and the חכמים use a lottery on שמיני עצרת. רבי uses all the watches, and the חכמים use only the two that brought two פרים.

steps.title: Does the ברייתא about two watches follow only רבי?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says every watch brings bulls twice and three times except two watches that bring only twice. The גמרא suggests this fits רבי, not the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view does this ברייתא follow: 'All the watches bring twice and three times, except two watches that bring twice and not three times'? Shall we say רבי and not the חכמים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same kind of question about a different ברייתא. That ברייתא says two watches never reach three bulls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the חכמים, one of those two watches gets the שמיני עצרת bull and so does reach three. A ברייתא saying two watches stay at two therefore seems to fit only רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: Do it a second and a third time

phrases.english: According to whom is this baraita that teaches:
all the watches do it twice and three times,
except for two watches
that do it twice but not three times?
Shall we say it is Rabbi and not the Rabbis!

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן אָזְלָא הָא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same מחלוקת from step 8 to test a second ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the 'two watches never bring three' ברייתא contradicts the חכמים.

steps.title: 'Not three times' means only during סוכות
steps.stepSummary: Even the חכמים agree with that ברייתא, because it only counts the פרים of the seven days of סוכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows the חכמים. What does 'did not bring three' mean? Among the bulls of the חג.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the ברייתא so that it fits the חכמים as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא counts only the 70 פרים of סוכות, where two watches really do stop at two. The extra bull of שמיני עצרת is not part of that count, so the חכמים have no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: The bulls of the seven days of סוכות

phrases.english: You can even say it is the Rabbis:
what does 'they did not do it three times' mean —
among the bulls of the Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן: מַאי לֹא שִׁלְּשׁוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 by narrowing what the ברייתא is counting.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the ברייתא's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא counts all bulls, including שמיני עצרת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא counts only the 70 פרים of סוכות.

steps.title: Isn't that just simple math?
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא only counts the פרים of סוכות, what does it teach? Dividing 70 bulls among 24 watches gives this result anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is it teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation it just gave, because the ברייתא now seems to say something obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Twenty-four watches times three is 72, which is two more than 70. So everyone already knows that two watches bring only two פרים, and a ברייתא would not need to say it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it teaching us? (implying the point is obvious)

phrases.english: And what is it teaching us!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading given in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא as explained in step 11.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that reading the ברייתא only states an obvious math result.

steps.title: The new point: the watches rotate
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא teaches the rotation rule. A watch that brought פרים today does not bring them tomorrow, so the turns go around in order and nobody gets a double share.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it teaches us: one who brought bulls today does not bring them tomorrow. Rather, they rotate in turn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is teaching the rule that the watches take turns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the rotation rule, the lottery could give one watch many bulls and leave others with fewer than two. The rotation is what guarantees that every watch brings at least two and most bring three. The גמרא is repeating the משנה's line here for a new purpose: to explain what the ברייתא adds.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us

steps.confusionAlert: This line repeats the words of the משנה from step 6. Here it does a new job: it shows what the ברייתא's count is teaching.
steps.whatToRemember: The count 'two watches bring twice, the rest three times' only works because of the rotation rule. A watch that brought פרים today waits until the others have had their turn.

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us:
one who offered bulls today —
will not offer tomorrow,
rather, they rotate in turn.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן: מִי שֶׁהִקְרִיב פָּרִים הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the hidden point of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא only states simple math.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא teaches that the watches rotate, which is what makes the count work.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The watches rotate, so no watch repeats the פרים until the others have had their turn.

steps.title: The 70 bulls stand for the 70 nations
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that the 70 פרים of סוכות correspond to the 70 nations of the world, and the single פר of שמיני עצרת corresponds to the one special nation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: These seventy bulls, whom do they stand for? They stand for the seventy nations. Why is there a single bull? It stands for the single, unique nation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the technical rules of the משמרות to a deeper meaning behind the number of bulls offered on סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Over the seven days of סוכות a total of 70 פרים are offered, and רבי אלעזר links them to the 70 nations of the world. On שמיני עצרת only one פר is offered, and that one stands for ישראל, the unique nation.

keyTerms.meaning: The seventy bulls offered over the seven days of סוכות (13 on the first day, then one fewer each day down to 7)
The seventy nations of the world
The single bull offered on שמיני עצרת

steps.whyThisMatters: It gives a spiritual reason for the unusual pattern of offerings: סוכות includes the whole world, while שמיני עצרת is a private holiday between הקב"ה and ישראל.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
These seventy bulls, whom do they correspond to?
phrases.notes: The bulls offered during the seven days of סוכות.

phrases.english: They correspond to the seventy nations.
Why is there a single bull?
phrases.notes: The one bull of שמיני עצרת.

phrases.english: It corresponds to the single, unique nation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי (אֶלְעָזָר): הָנֵי שִׁבְעִים פָּרִים כְּנֶגֶד מִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the technical discussion of dividing the 70 פרים among the משמרות, the גמרא now explains what those 70 bulls mean.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The 70 פרים of סוכות correspond to the 70 nations, and the single פר of שמיני עצרת corresponds to ישראל.

steps.title: Parable of the king's great feast and small feast
steps.stepSummary: A parable explains the single bull of שמיני עצרת: a king holds a big feast for everyone, then asks his beloved friend for a small, private meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like a human king who told his servants: Make me a great feast. On the last day he said to his beloved friend: Make me a small meal, so that I can enjoy your company alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a parable to illustrate רבי אלעזר's idea about the 70 bulls and the single bull.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The great feast stands for the seven days of סוכות, with 70 bulls for all the nations. The small meal on the last day stands for שמיני עצרת, with one bull, a private moment between the King and His beloved, ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: A human king, literally a king of flesh and blood
So that I may enjoy you, meaning your company alone

phrases.english: A parable: it is like a king of flesh and blood
who said to his servants:
Make me a great feast.
phrases.notes: Like the seven days of סוכות with many bulls.

phrases.english: On the last day he said to his beloved friend:
Make me a small meal
phrases.notes: Like שמיני עצרת with its single bull.

phrases.english: so that I may enjoy your company alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָשָׁל לְמֶלֶךְ בָּשָׂר וָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates רבי אלעזר's teaching with a parable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The single bull of שמיני עצרת is like a small private meal the king shares only with his beloved.

steps.title: The nations lost their atonement without knowing it
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן laments that while the בית המקדש stood, the מזבח atoned for the nations through the 70 bulls, and now nothing atones for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Woe to the nations, who lost something and do not know what they lost. When the בית המקדש stood, the מזבח atoned for them. Now, who atones for them?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds to the idea that the 70 bulls are for the nations, and mourns what the nations lost when the בית המקדש was destroyed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the 70 פרים were offered for the 70 nations, then the מזבח was bringing atonement to the whole world. Once the בית המקדש was destroyed, that atonement stopped, and the nations do not even realize what they lost.
steps.whatToRemember: The 70 bulls of סוכות are for the 70 nations, and the one bull of שמיני עצרת is for ישראל. Through the מזבח, the nations also received atonement, and that was lost with the destruction of the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Woe to the nations, who lost something
and do not know what they lost.
When the Temple was standing,
the altar atoned for them.
phrases.notes: Through the 70 bulls offered on סוכות.

phrases.english: And now, who atones for them?!
phrases.notes: A cry of sorrow, not a question waiting for an answer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אוֹי לָהֶם לַגּוֹיִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי אלעזר's idea that the 70 bulls are for the nations and draws out a sad result for the time after the destruction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: While the בית המקדש stood, the מזבח atoned for the nations. After its destruction they have lost that atonement without realizing it.

steps.title: New משנה: all the משמרות share equally on the three רגלים
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that on the three festivals, all 24 משמרות are equal: they all share in the festival offerings and in the distribution of the לחם הפנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: At three times in the year, all the משמרות were equal: in the parts of the festival offerings, and in the dividing of the לחם הפנים.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets out a rule about how the כהנים of all the משמרות shared on the רגלים, and the גמרא will discuss it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually only the משמר on duty that week served in the בית המקדש and received the gifts. On the three רגלים, when all the כהנים came to ירושלים, every משמר had an equal share in the festival offerings and in the לחם הפנים given out on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Three times, meaning the three festivals: פסח, שבועות, סוכות
The 24 rotating groups of כהנים, each serving one week at a time
The offerings of the festivals, which all the משמרות shared
The showbread, divided among the כהנים every שבת

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse this with the earlier rule about rotating the 70 bulls. That rule decided which watch brings which animal during סוכות, and all 24 משמרות were already serving then too. This new משנה is about sharing the gifts the כהנים receive on all three רגלים: the festival portions and the לחם הפנים.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
At three times in the year
all the priestly watches were equal:
in the offerings of the festivals,
phrases.notes: All the משמרות served and shared in the festival offerings.

phrases.english: and in the distribution of the showbread.
phrases.notes: On a שבת that fell during the רגל.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה פְּרָקִים בַּשָּׁנָה הָיוּ כׇּל מִשְׁמָרוֹת שָׁווֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה opens a new topic after the aggadic close of the previous discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the three רגלים, all 24 משמרות share equally in the festival offerings and in the distribution of the לחם הפנים.

steps.title: On שבועות, each כהן gets מצה and חמץ
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends its case of עצרת falling on שבת: the person handing out the bread says, 'Here is מצה, here is חמץ.'
steps.simpleTranslation: On עצרת (when it falls on שבת), he says to each כהן: 'Here is מצה for you, here is חמץ for you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its case: when שבועות falls on שבת, two kinds of bread are handed out at the same time, and each כהן receives both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת, the old לחם הפנים is handed out, and it is מצה. On שבועות, the שתי הלחם are handed out, and they are חמץ. When the two days fall together, every כהן gets a piece of each, and the watches share equally.

keyTerms.meaning: The name the משנה uses for שבועות
Unleavened bread (here, from the לחם הפנים)
Leavened bread (here, from the שתי הלחם of שבועות)

steps.confusionAlert: The חמץ is not from the לחם הפנים. The לחם הפנים is always מצה. The חמץ comes from the שתי הלחם, which are brought only on שבועות.

phrases.english: On Shavuot (falling on Shabbat), he says to him:
phrases.notes: When שבועות falls on שבת, the שתי הלחם and the לחם הפנים get handed out together.

phrases.english: Here is matzah for you,
here is leavened bread for you.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֲצֶרֶת, אוֹמֵר לוֹ: הֵילָךְ מַצָּה, הֵילָךְ חָמֵץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה's case of equal sharing among all watches
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When עצרת falls on שבת, each כהן receives both מצה (לחם הפנים) and חמץ (שתי הלחם).

steps.title: The scheduled watch keeps the regular offerings
steps.stepSummary: The watch whose turn falls during the festival still brings the תמידין, the private offerings, and the other communal offerings by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The watch whose time is fixed brings the daily offerings, the vow-offerings and gift-offerings, and the other communal offerings. It brings all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sets a limit: the equal sharing applies only to festival items. The regular service still belongs to the watch whose week it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All 24 watches share only what belongs to the festival itself. Anything that would be brought on a normal day stays with the scheduled watch, even during the רגל.

keyTerms.meaning: The watch whose regular week it is
The daily offerings, brought morning and afternoon
Private offerings that someone pledged or donated
Offerings brought for the whole community

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the festival does not cancel the regular schedule. It only adds a shared layer on top of it.

phrases.english: The watch whose time is fixed,
it offers the daily offerings,
vow-offerings and free-will offerings,
and the other communal offerings —
and it offers all of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשְׁמָר שֶׁזְּמַנּוֹ קָבוּעַ, הוּא מַקְרִיב תְּמִידִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the equal-sharing rule of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Non-festival offerings stay with the scheduled watch, even during the רגל.

steps.title: Festival portions go on the altar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: אימורים are burned on the מזבח for ה׳, so how can the כהנים divide them?
steps.simpleTranslation: The portions of the festival offerings belong to ה׳!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by challenging a word in the משנה. אימורים are burned on the מזבח, so there is nothing left for the כהנים to share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual meaning of אימורים is the fats and parts that go on the מזבח. If that is what the משנה means, its statement about the כהנים sharing them makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Parts of an offering that are burned on the מזבח
'The One on High,' meaning ה׳ (things that belong to the מזבח)

phrases.english: Gemara:
The portions of the festival offerings
belong to the Most High!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימוּרֵי הָרְגָלִים שֶׁל גָּבוֹהַּ נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the משנה quoted in step 17
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אימורים are burned on the מזבח, so the כהנים cannot divide them.

steps.title: רב חסדא: it means what is stated for the festivals
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא reads the word as 'אמור,' meaning the portions stated for the רגלים that the כהנים receive, not the altar parts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It means 'what is stated for the festivals.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers by reading the word differently. It is not the altar parts but 'what is said' about the festivals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads אימורי as coming from אמור, 'stated.' The משנה means the festival portions that go to the כהנים, such as the hides of the עולות and the chest and thigh of the שלמים. These can be divided.

keyTerms.meaning: What is stated (a wordplay on אימורים)

steps.confusionAlert: רב חסדא is not changing the text of the משנה. He keeps the same word and gives it a different meaning.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
What is stated regarding the festivals.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מַה שֶּׁאָמוּר בָּרְגָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 20
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אימורים means the altar parts, which cannot be shared.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means the festival portions given to the כהנים, which can be shared.

steps.title: Source that all watches share the festival portions
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא proves from the verse 'ובא בכל אות נפשו ושרת' that all the watches share equally in the festival portions.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: How do we know that all the watches are equal in the festival portions? The verse says: 'And he comes with all the desire of his soul and serves.'
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא gives the Torah source for the משנה's rule. Any כהן who comes may serve and take a share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says a כהן who comes 'with all his desire' may serve, and the passage goes on to say he gets an equal portion. So even a כהן from another watch shares in the festival offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: How do we know? (asks for a source)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
From where do we know that all the watches
are equal in the festival portions?
The verse states:
'And he comes with all the desire of his soul ... and serves.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִנַּיִן שֶׁכׇּל הַמִּשְׁמָרוֹת שָׁווֹת בְּאֵימוּרֵי הָרְגָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining the term, the גמרא gives the Torah source for the rule
steps.raayaObject: All watches share equally in the festival portions
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים י״ח:ו׳–ז׳, 'ובא בכל אות נפשו ושרת'

steps.title: Maybe this applies all year
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that perhaps the verse lets any watch share all year round.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think it is the same on the other days of the year too.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible wrong reading of the verse. This sets up the limiting verse in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse 'ובא בכל אות נפשו' does not mention a time. On its own, it could mean any כהן may come and share on any day, which would cancel the watch system.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think (introduces a possible wrong reading)
The rest of the days of the year

phrases.english: One might think that even on the rest
of the days of the year it is so —

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל אַף בִּשְׁאָר יְמוֹת הַשָּׁנָה כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far the verse in step 22 reaches
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the equal sharing apply all year?

steps.title: Only when all Israel enters through one gate
steps.stepSummary: The verse 'מאחד שעריך' limits equal sharing to the רגלים, when all of Israel gathers in one place.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'From one of your gates.' I said this only at a time when all of Israel enters through one gate.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with a phrase from the same passage that limits the rule to the festivals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'From one of your gates' is read as a time when everyone comes through one gate, meaning the רגלים, when all of ישראל goes up to ירושלים. During the rest of the year, the watch system stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: I said it only (limits the rule)
One gate, a picture of everyone gathering together

steps.whatToRemember: All 24 watches share the festival portions only on the רגלים, the time when all of Israel 'enters through one gate.' The rest of the year, each watch keeps its own turn.

phrases.english: The verse states:
'From one of your gates,'
I said this only at a time
when all of Israel enters
through one gate.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״מֵאַחַד שְׁעָרֶיךָ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 23
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. The phrase 'מאחד שעריך' limits equal sharing to the רגלים.

steps.title: Source for sharing the showbread
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה, about the לחם הפנים, and a ברייתא begins asking for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And in the distribution of the לחם הפנים, etc.' The Rabbis taught: How do we know that all the watches are equal in the distribution of the לחם הפנים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next phrase of the משנה and asks for its source. This sets up the answer on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse already showed that the watches share the festival offerings. The לחם הפנים is not a festival offering, so it needs its own source.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Etc.', marking a shortened quote from the משנה

phrases.english: 'And in the distribution of the showbread, etc.'
The Rabbis taught:
From where do we know that all the watches
are equal in the distribution of the showbread —

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְחִילּוּק לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the festival portions to the second item in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source that all watches share the לחם הפנים on the רגלים
